candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — losartan use in proteinuric diabetic nephropathy
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize the labeled renal-protective indication of losartan in hypertensive type 2 diabetic nephropathy with proteinuria while understanding that treatment slows progression rather than curing CKD.

options.A: Losartan has a labeled diabetic-nephropathy indication in this population and can reduce the rate of kidney-disease progression, including progression to doubling of serum creatinine or end-stage renal disease.
options.B: Losartan is contraindicated whenever chronic kidney disease is present because angiotensin-receptor blockers always accelerate renal failure.
options.C: Losartan is used only to lower blood pressure and has no labeled renal-outcome indication in type 2 diabetic nephropathy.
options.D: Losartan cures the underlying diabetic kidney disease, so renal-function and potassium monitoring are unnecessary after therapy begins.

candidate.rationale: Current FDA labeling indicates losartan for diabetic nephropathy with elevated serum creatinine and proteinuria in patients with type 2 diabetes and a history of hypertension. In this population, losartan reduces the rate of progression of nephropathy as measured by doubling of serum creatinine or end-stage renal disease requiring dialysis or transplantation. It does not cure CKD, and the label includes warnings regarding renal-function deterioration and hyperkalemia, so monitoring remains important. Therefore, A is correct; B, C, and D contradict the current prescribing information.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports losartan's drug-specific diabetic-nephropathy indication and renal-progression outcome while also supporting continued renal-function/potassium safety monitoring.
